data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all AUR repository files (.gitignore, .SRCINFO, PKGBUILD) and found them to be standard, safe packaging files. The PKGBUILD downloads a pinned source tarball from the official GitHub repository and builds it using standard Rust/cargo commands. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict was solely due to an API error (HTTP 400) during the file review phase, not a security finding. Its initial PKGBUILD parse also found no malicious global scope code.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is caused by a tool error in the qwen model. It failed to review .gitignore and PKGBUILD due to an HTTP 400 API error, resulting in an inconclusive verdict, whereas deepseek successfully reviewed all files and found them safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore and PKGBUILD due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError).
learnings: Handle LLM API errors (like HTTP 400) during file review gracefully. If the initial PKGBUILD audit passes and subsequent file reviews fail due to API errors, the tool should either retry the failed files or rely on the initial audit and other models' successful reviews rather than defaulting to an inconclusive verdict for the whole package.
